days.rationale: Hydrated storage shows a +149 Bcf five-year surplus with a +45 Bcf prior build, while nuclear outages are already elevated. Those forces oppose each other; without weekend/weather/tape evidence B keeps the S129 -250 p50 and abstains.

The storage surplus and South Central/salt spare capacity keep the shoulder balance loose. Nuclear outages eased from the prior read and no price/tape delivery exists, so C increases the weak-down magnitude to -400 but keeps confidence low.

The Sep STEO becomes knowable: September demand and power burn are marked below August while production is nearly flat and working gas is rising. That reinforces the existing downside chain; nuclear outages partly offset it, yielding -400 rather than a full bearish extension.

Nuclear outages jump above 7.5 GW and rise more than 1 GW day over day, a real bullish gas-burn offset to the loose storage/STEO backdrop. C retains the S129 covering-up sign but trims it to +175 because the physical balance remains loose.

Nuclear outages remain above 7.6 GW and day length continues falling, supporting gas burn, but the Sep storage surplus and lower STEO power-burn baseline remain a counterweight. C keeps a small +75 covering drift only.

Storage Thursday is still directionally underdetermined without D-1 tape or same-print consensus. Nuclear outages near 8 GW oppose the loose storage/STEO state, so D keeps a downside stress path near the S129 prior (-500) and abstains.
